section: Fiscal decentralisation to local bodies - State Finance Commissions and local revenue
subsections: Eleventh and Twelfth Schedules - the 3F mismatch
Challenges - property tax, dependence, delayed SFCs

accepted.s: The Eleventh Schedule of the Constitution is associated with which of the following?
accepted.x: The Eleventh Schedule relates to Panchayats and contains 29 subjects under Article 243G.
accepted.tq: Use the schedule-article-subject association to eliminate reversed combinations.
accepted.sec: Eleventh and Twelfth Schedules - the 3F mismatch

accepted.s: The Twelfth Schedule deals with which of the following combinations?
accepted.x: The Twelfth Schedule concerns municipalities and contains 18 subjects under Article 243W.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the closely related Eleventh and Twelfth Schedule provisions.
accepted.sec: Eleventh and Twelfth Schedules - the 3F mismatch

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the three Fs of local-body fiscal decentralisation:
1. The three Fs are Functions, Funds and Functionaries.
2. Functions may be devolved on paper while funds remain tied to schemes.
3. Staff may continue to report to State line departments.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The three Fs are Functions, Funds and Functionaries; the mismatch arises when functions are devolved, funds are tied to schemes and staff remain accountable to State departments.
accepted.tq: Check each component of the three-F framework before selecting the combined option.
accepted.sec: Eleventh and Twelfth Schedules - the 3F mismatch

accepted.s: The mismatch among Functions, Funds and Functionaries tends to reduce Panchayati Raj Institutions primarily to the role of:
accepted.x: When local bodies lack adequate untied funds and control over personnel, PRIs are reduced largely to implementing agencies.
accepted.tq: Apply the institutional consequence of an incomplete devolution of powers.
accepted.sec: Eleventh and Twelfth Schedules - the 3F mismatch

accepted.s: According to the IIHS study covering 80 urban local bodies during 2012–17, intergovernmental transfers accounted for approximately what share of ULB revenue?
accepted.x: The IIHS study reported that intergovernmental transfers constituted about 40 percent of ULB revenue.
accepted.tq: Identify the reported percentage and distinguish it from nearby round-number distractors.
accepted.sec: Challenges - property tax, dependence, delayed SFCs

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly compares India’s intergovernmental transfers with the global norm mentioned for such transfers?
o: India: about 5% of GDP; global norm: 0.5–1% of GDP
India: about 0.5% of GDP; global norm: 2–5% of GDP
India: about 1–2% of GDP; global norm: 3–4% of GDP
India: about 2–5% of GDP; global norm: 0.5% of GDP
accepted.x: India’s intergovernmental transfers are about 0.5 percent of GDP, compared with a global norm of roughly 2–5 percent of GDP.
accepted.tq: Split the comparison into the India figure and the global range before choosing.
accepted.sec: Challenges - property tax, dependence, delayed SFCs

accepted.s:
With reference to the dependence of urban local bodies on intergovernmental transfers, consider the following statements:
1. Class I-A cities with a population of 50 lakh or more reduced their dependence from 27 percent to 15 percent.
2. Smaller cities remained grant-dependent.
3. The reduction in dependence was reported uniformly across all categories of cities.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The reduction was specifically observed in Class I-A cities, while smaller cities remained grant-dependent; it was not uniform across all categories.
accepted.tq: Reject the overgeneralisation in the statement using the comparison between large and smaller cities.
accepted.sec: Challenges - property tax, dependence, delayed SFCs

accepted.s: Which of the following is identified as a barrier to local bodies’ access to the bond market?
o: Excessive accrual accounting and strong balance sheets
Absence of accrual accounting and weak balance sheets
Complete dependence on property tax surpluses
Excessive control over State line-department staff
accepted.x: The absence of accrual accounting and weak balance sheets restrict local bodies’ access to the bond market.
accepted.tq: Match the institutional weakness with its stated financial-market consequence.
accepted.sec: Challenges - property tax, dependence, delayed SFCs

accepted.s: Which institutional measure has been called for to support genuine three-tier fiscal federalism?
o: Replacement of local bodies by Special Officers permanently
Exclusive financing of local bodies through municipal bonds
Regular constitution of State Finance Commissions
accepted.x: Regular constitution of State Finance Commissions has been called for as part of genuine three-tier fiscal federalism.
accepted.tq: Identify the institutional reform directly linked with fiscal federalism.
accepted.sec: Challenges - property tax, dependence, delayed SFCs

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the Sixteenth Finance Commission grants to Andhra Pradesh.

List-I (Local body category)
a. Rural local bodies
b. Urban local bodies
c. Vijayawada

d. Visakhapatnam

List-II (Provision)
i. ₹12,158 crore over 2026–31
ii. ₹16,627 crore over 2026–31
iii. Eligible for up to ₹5,000 crore for wastewater
a. Eligible for up to ₹5,000 crore for wastewater

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Rural local bodies were allocated ₹16,627 crore and urban local bodies ₹12,158 crore for 2026–31. Both Vijayawada and Visakhapatnam are eligible for up to ₹5,000 crore each for wastewater; in the matching, c–iii and d–iv represent these two identical provisions.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure rural–urban grant pairs, then assign the two identical city provisions.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding local bodies in Andhra Pradesh in 2026:
1. The terms of AP urban local bodies expired on 15 March 2026.
2. The terms of the panchayats expired on 4 April 2026.
3. The terms of MPPs and ZPPs were due to expire on 23 September 2026.
4. Special Officers were running the local bodies after the expiry of their terms.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct: ULB terms ended on 15 March 2026, panchayat terms on 4 April 2026, MPPs/ZPPs were due by 23 September 2026, and Special Officers were administering the bodies.
accepted.tq: Verify each date and the administrative consequence before selecting the inclusive option.

accepted.s: Why does the delay in holding local-body elections in Andhra Pradesh put Finance Commission grants at risk?
o: Grants require only an increase in property-tax rates.
Grants are available only to municipalities with bond-market access.
Grants are linked to elected bodies, audited accounts and compliance with State Finance Commission requirements.
Grants require the abolition of Special Officers before the preparation of any budget.
accepted.x: The grants are linked to the existence of elected bodies, audited accounts and compliance with State Finance Commission requirements. Delays therefore jeopardise eligibility and release of grants.
accepted.tq: Link the administrative delay to the stated grant-eligibility conditions.

accepted.s: Which of the following conditions was associated with the Sixteenth Finance Commission’s local-body grants?
o: Only population size and geographical area
Appointment of Special Officers for every local body
Elected local bodies, audited accounts and State Finance Commission compliance
accepted.x: The conditions include elected bodies, audited accounts and compliance with State Finance Commission requirements.
accepted.tq: Select the option containing the complete set of grant-linked conditions.

accepted.s: The linking of local-body grants to elected bodies, accounts and State Finance Commission compliance has been criticised by some as:
o: A constitutional abolition of local self-government
A replacement of fiscal federalism by monetary policy
A complete withdrawal from fiscal federalism
accepted.x: Critics have described the conditional design of the grants as a re-engineering of fiscal federalism.
accepted.tq: Recognise the precise evaluative expression associated with the policy design.

accepted.s: In the context of Andhra Pradesh, the dependence of Sixteenth Finance Commission grants on the holding of local-body elections means that:
o: Delayed elections may affect access to the grants.
Special Officers automatically qualify local bodies for all grants.
Only urban local bodies can receive the grants.
Audited accounts are no longer relevant for grant release.
accepted.x: Since grant access is linked to elected local bodies, the operation of local bodies under Special Officers after delayed elections may affect eligibility for the grants.
accepted.tq: Apply the grant condition to the specific situation of local bodies under Special Officers.
